why: On 2026-09-06 public/interop/agent-card-jws-input.json described a card nobody served. Its producer was correct; nothing re-ran it. The whole gates job was red for every lane until someone noticed. This manifest names source -> producer -> output so CI can notice instead.
how_to_read: Each entry names what a producer WRITES and how to prove the committed bytes still match. `gated: true` entries are enforced by scripts/producers-check.mjs in CI. `gated: false` entries record WHY they cannot be, which is the more useful half.
extending: Add an entry, run `node scripts/producers-check.mjs` locally, and only set gated:true once it passes on a clean tree. Never set gated:true on a producer that stamps a timestamp or a random id into its output, and never on one that signs.

producers.verified_2026_09_06: re-run on a clean tree changed 0 files; no timestamp, no network, no signing key
producers.note: THE ONE THAT BROKE. Deterministic and offline, which is why regenerating it needed no key and cost nothing.

producers.reason: Reads another GIT BRANCH: `git show os-production:<path>` and `git diff origin/master...os-production`. The gates job uses actions/checkout@v4 with no fetch-depth, i.e. a depth-1 SINGLE-BRANCH clone, so origin/os-production does not exist there and the script exits non-zero. It passes on a developer clone, which has every branch — that difference is exactly why it was wrongly gated first.
producers.do_not_fix_by: Adding fetch-depth: 0 to make this one step pass. That slows every CI run for every lane to satisfy one gate, and gates are never widened to make a tip deployable. Gate it in the harness lane's own workflow, where the branch is already fetched.
producers.observed_2026_09_06: passes locally (35 staged, 13 quarantined); FAILS in CI — origin/os-production absent

producers.reason: NOT byte-diffable: the producer stamps a fresh `metadata.timestamp` and a RANDOM `serialNumber` (urn:uuid:<random>-councilof-ai) on every run, so a re-run-and-diff gate would be permanently red.
producers.drift_found_2026_09_06: The committed SBOM is dated 2026-08-25T13:20:09Z and lists 126 components; a fresh run emits 120. The published supply-chain artefact overstates the dependency set by 6 and is 12 days stale. A count/name-set comparison ignoring timestamp and serialNumber WOULD be gateable and is the recommended follow-up.

producers.reason: Already gated separately in pr-gates.yml, and its --check fetches the LIVE board, so running it here too would double-spend the <=20/hour self-probe budget for no extra coverage.
Environment-dependent: reports CANNOT-RUN when a local TypeScript compiler is absent. A gate that is red for a missing tool teaches people to ignore it.

These SIGN. Re-running them needs private keys that are deliberately not in CI, and a signature over freshly serialised bytes differs from the published one even when the content is identical. Signed bytes are superseded or ledgered, never regenerated to make a gate pass.

not_yet_classified.note: About 40 scripts under scripts/ write into public/. The 11 entries above are the ones actually RUN and observed on 2026-09-06. The rest are unclassified rather than assumed safe, because guessing a producer is deterministic and gating it is how a permanently-red gate gets shipped.
